system.summary: Sphingolipid metabolism in mammalian cells is a well-mapped, essentially linear-with-branches network whose topology is not in dispute, even though almost no rate constants exist for human neuroblastoma. De novo synthesis condenses palmitoyl-CoA with L-serine (SPT, R-HSA-428127) and reduces the 3-ketosphinganine product (KDSR, R-HSA-428123) to sphinganine; ceramide synthases N-acylate sphinganine to dihydroceramide (R-HSA-428185); DEGS1 desaturates it to ceramide (R-HSA-428259). Ceramide is the hub: sphingomyelin synthases transfer phosphocholine from PC onto ceramide, releasing diacylglycerol (R-HSA-429798, R-HSA-429786) — a reaction Reactome states is reversible — sphingomyelinases run the reverse hydrolysis (R-HSA-1605797, R-HSA-1606273), UGCG glucosylates ceramide (R-HSA-1638104), and ceramidases hydrolyse ceramide to a free sphingoid base plus a free fatty acid (R-HSA-1606602, R-HSA-428205, R-HSA-428231). The only exit from the sphingoid backbone is phosphorylation by sphingosine kinases (R-HSA-428273), reversible by SGPP1/2 (R-HSA-428664), followed by irreversible SGPL1 cleavage to hexadecenal (from S1P) or hexadecanal (from sphinganine-1-phosphate) plus phosphoethanolamine (R-HSA-428681); aldehyde dehydrogenases then oxidise those aldehydes to palmitate (R-HSA-5692261, R-HSA-5696080, R-HSA-6808464), which is how sphingoid-base label enters the free-fatty-acid and glycerolipid pools. That last route is demonstrated directly with a clickable sphingoid base: about half of pacSph became PC within 4 h in Sgpl1+/+ MEFs and no glycerolipid labelling at all occurred in Sgpl1-/- cells (Gerl 2016). Three structural points bear directly on the user's base model and on its non-sphingolipid pools. First, SM formation is not a unimolecular Cer -> SM step: it consumes PC and produces DG stoichiometrically, which is a mechanistic coupling between the sphingolipid branch and the fitted PC and DG pools. Second, sphingomyelin synthase and UGCG also accept dihydroceramide, so the measured SM and HexCer classes contain dihydro-species and a DhCer -> SM / DhCer -> HexCer shortcut is chemically real. Third, the canonical route out of ceramide other than SM and HexCer is ceramidase, whose product is sphingosine (d18:1), a species distinct from sphinganine and absent from both the base model and the fitted data; without it there is no literature route by which the base model can produce S1P and hence hexadecenal. On the glycerolipid side, alkyne fatty acid tracing in the same click-MS platform shows label entering PA and DG first and only then TG and PC, i.e. DG is an obligate precursor of PC rather than a parallel branch off the FFA pool.
system.scope: Human generic pathway annotation (Reactome, Homo sapiens); experimental tracer work in mouse embryonic fibroblasts (Sgpl1+/+ and Sgpl1-/-), human Huh7 hepatoma, mouse hepatocytes and 3T3-L1 adipocytes; kinetic modelling in RAW264.7 mouse macrophages. Compartments: ER (SPT, KDSR, CerS, DEGS1, ACER1), Golgi (SGMS1, UGCG, ACER2), plasma membrane and lysosome (SMPD1/2/3, ASAH1/2), cytosol/ER for SPHK, SGPP and SGPL1. Conditions: unstimulated cultured cells unless stated. No source found that uses the intent's exact system (SH-SY5Y, basal, 1 uM alkyne sphinganine plus 50 uM 13C6-alkyne palmitate, 60 min pulse / 180 min chase).
unknowns: No rate constants for any sphingolipid step in SH-SY5Y or any human neuroblastoma line were found; the only fitted mass-action constants located are for the C16 branch in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 mouse macrophages.

No published mechanistic model of mammalian sphingolipid metabolism fitted to click-chemistry alkyne tracer pulse-chase data was found; existing models are fitted to steady-state or stimulus-response lipidomics, not to label chase.

Sphingosine (d18:1), the obligatory product of ceramidase and the substrate whose phosphorylation yields S1P and hence hexadecenal, is neither a species of the base model nor a fitted pool; whether the measured 'sphinganine' pool in this dataset also contains d18:1 sphingosine could not be determined from the lab note.

The lab note reports that most hexadecenal and hexadecanal label is palmitate-derived. The curated direction of ALDH3A2/ALDH3B1/ALDH3B2 is aldehyde -> palmitate, not palmitate -> aldehyde, so no canonical route was found that would put palmitate label into these aldehydes; this conflict is unresolved.

Whether the constant influx term into the FFA pool corresponds to a real process during a chase is not settled by literature: recycling from stored neutral lipid is documented (TG half-life 2-4 h in adipocytes), but no measurement of that flux in SH-SY5Y was found.

The partitioning of hexosylceramide between glucosylceramide (UGCG) and galactosylceramide (UGT8), and the magnitude of the drain from HexCer into lactosylceramide and gangliosides in SH-SY5Y specifically, were not found quantitatively.
Absolute basal pool sizes (pmol per cell or per mg protein) for Sph, DhCer, Cer, SM and HexCer in SH-SY5Y under the stated growth conditions were not found.

facts.statement: The sphingolipid pathway is split across organelles - SPT, KDSR, CerS, DEGS1 and ACER1 at the ER, SGMS1, UGCG and ACER2 at the Golgi, SMPD1/ASAH1 in the lysosome, SMPD2/3 and ASAH2 at the plasma membrane, SPHK1 in the cytosol and SGPL1 at the ER - so a single-compartment model collapses the ER-to-Golgi ceramide transport step (CERT and vesicular transport) that separates ceramide synthesis from SM and HexCer synthesis.

evidence.title: SGMS1 transfers phosphocholine onto ceramide
evidence.locator: Reactome reaction entry, compartment annotation of inputs, outputs and catalyst
evidence.supports: The SM-forming reaction is annotated entirely in the Golgi membrane, whereas the de novo reactions (R-HSA-428127, R-HSA-428123, R-HSA-428185, R-HSA-428259) are annotated at the ER, establishing the compartment separation that the single-compartment model collapses.
evidence.context_note: Reactome Homo sapiens generic annotation, not SH-SY5Y specific.
evidence.second_note: No excerpt supplied; item states Reactome compartment annotations (Golgi membrane for SGMS1 versus ER for the de novo steps) — the comparison across entries is the item's, from curated location fields.

evidence.title: Structure, functions and regulation of CERT, a lipid-transfer protein for the delivery of ceramide at the ER-Golgi membrane contact sites
evidence.locator: Review, CERT-mediated ER-to-Golgi ceramide transfer
evidence.supports: CERT transports ceramide from the ER to the trans-Golgi at membrane contact sites, a prerequisite step for conversion of ceramide into sphingomyelin; this transport step is absent from a single-compartment model and is a candidate explanation for any delay between ceramide labelling and SM labelling.
evidence.context_note: Review of mammalian CERT biology; no quantitative transfer half-time in SH-SY5Y was found in the accessible text.
evidence.second_note: No excerpt supplied; item describes a review of CERT-mediated ER-to-Golgi ceramide transfer and notes no quantitative transfer half-time was found.

facts.statement: In neural cells hexosylceramide is not an end product: glucosylceramide is converted to lactosylceramide, which is a branch point serving at least six glycosyltransferases and a sulfotransferase and feeding the a-, b- and c-series gangliosides, so a continuing drain out of the measured HexCer pool into unmeasured glycosphingolipids is expected.

evidence.supports: Describes the stepwise conversion of glucosylceramide to lactosylceramide and on to the ganglioside series by up to six further glycosyltransferases, with lactosylceramide as a major branch point.
evidence.context_note: Review of mammalian, largely neuronal, ganglioside metabolism; no SH-SY5Y flux measurement under the intent's conditions.
evidence.second_note: No excerpt supplied; item describes a review section on stepwise GlcCer -> LacCer -> ganglioside glycosylation with LacCer as a branch point.

facts.statement: The sphingoid base released by ceramidase is sphingosine (d18:1), a species distinct from sphinganine (d18:0); a model with a single sphingoid-base pool therefore either loses the ceramide-to-base route or misassigns its product, and the sphingosine pool is not among the eleven fitted pools, so it would be an unobserved state.

facts.statement: The curated direction of fatty aldehyde metabolism is hexadecenal or hexadecanal to palmitate, not palmitate to aldehyde, so no canonical route was found that would place palmitate-derived label into the measured hexadecenal and hexadecanal pools; the lab note's observation that most aldehyde label is palmitate-derived is therefore unexplained by the pathway as curated.

evidence.second_note: No excerpt supplied; item states the Reactome entry annotates only hexadec-2-enal -> palmitate, so the reverse direction is unannotated — contradicting palmitate label entering the aldehyde pool by this route.

notes: COVERAGE GAPS. (1) No study was found that uses the intent's system - SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma, basal, dual alkyne sphinganine plus 13C6-alkyne palmitate pulse-chase with click-MS. Every evidence item is therefore classified related_system or different_system; none is same_system. The closest matches on tracer chemistry and instrument platform (Thiele 2019, Frontiers 2022, Wunderling 2023) are in mouse hepatocytes and adipocytes; the closest match on clickable sphingoid-base tracing (Gerl 2016 in MEFs, Hoglinger-lab trifunctional sphinganine 2024 in Huh7) is in other cell types. (2) No rate constant for any sphingolipid step in SH-SY5Y or any human neuroblastoma line was found. The only fitted mass-action constants located are Gupta et al. 2011 for the C16 branch in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 mouse macrophages, and their units are model-specific (some carry a ug DNA normalisation), so they are order-of-magnitude guidance only, not transferable priors. Chiappa et al. 2025 builds a comparable macrophage network but does not report fitted constants in the accessible text. (3) No published mechanistic model of mammalian sphingolipid metabolism fitted to click-chemistry tracer pulse-chase data was found; the existing models are fitted to concentration lipidomics. (4) No quantitative CERT-mediated ER-to-Golgi ceramide transfer half-time was found, so the delay collapsed by the single-compartment assumption cannot be bounded from literature. (5) No source was found for the error structure of this assay, so that fact is returned with evidence: []. (6) No absolute SH-SY5Y sphingolipid pool sizes were found, so that fact is returned with evidence: [] as well. CONFLICTS. (a) The lab note reports that most hexadecenal and hexadecanal label is palmitate-derived. Reactome annotates ALDH3A2, ALDH3B1 and ALDH3B2 only in the direction aldehyde to palmitate, so I found no canonical route producing these aldehydes from palmitate; both Reactome items are returned with stance: contradicts against the lab note's reading, and the point is repeated as an 'unknown' fact. (b) The base model's Cer -> SM is unimolecular, while the curated reaction consumes PC and releases DG; the Frontiers review's tracer ordering likewise contradicts a direct Pal -> PC step in favour of DG -> PC. Both contradicting items are returned with stance: contradicts on the base-model reactions they bear against, and the stoichiometrically complete alternatives are returned as separate non-essential reactions so they can be tested one at a time. STRUCTURAL POINTS THE ENGINE SHOULD SEE. The base model as described has no sphingosine (d18:1) species, yet it produces S1P and hexadecenal; the only literature route to S1P runs through ceramidase and sphingosine, so either a sphingosine pool is added (Cer -> So + Pal, So -> S1P, both returned essential) or the two steps are collapsed (Cer -> S1P + Pal, returned non-essential as the identifiability variant). Every reaction whose description begins 'COLLAPSED' names the literature steps it merges, as the success criteria require. IDENTIFIERS. Reactome identifiers were verified by fetching or by a Reactome-hosted search result for each one cited. I did not find a verifiable Reactome identifier for the GBA1/GBA2 glucosylceramidase reaction, so HexCer -> Cer is cited to a review instead. ChEBI identifiers are given only for the six species I am confident of and omitted elsewhere; no KEGG or Rhea identifiers are given because I could not verify them. The JLR 2020 chain-length flux paper returned HTTP 403, so it is cited at abstract level with no quote and with its cell line unconfirmed, and classified different_system for that reason. RESTRICTIONS. All cited sources are published 2007-2025, within the 2026 cutoff. None of the three excluded sources was consulted, cited or searched for.
